tossups.text: Dogs with this disease may receive injections of prednisolone or DOCP. It affects levels of the enzyme 21-hydroxylase and can rarely be caused by HIV or a certain kind of tuberculosis. Tests for this disease include long CRH stimulation tests and characteristic symptoms include hyperpigmentation of non-exposed skin. It results in insufficient secretions of the zona fasciculate and can result from withdrawal of glucocorticoid hormones such as prednisone. For 10 points, inadequate secretion of ACTH by the pituitary gland or a primarily adrenal insufficiency are the primary causes of what endocrine disorder that causes the adrenal glands to produce insufficient amounts of cortisol?

This place was swallowed by a hellmouth following the first season of the absurdist sports game Blaseball. Suelo, a "simple living" advocate who quit using money in 2000, lives part-time in a cave near this place. A DOE remediation program in this place is hauling 16 million tons of radioactive tailings to nearby Crescent Junction. A discovery by geologist Charlie Steen, who built the Atlas Mill in this place, led to it being named the "Uranium Capital of the World". A difficult mountain biking route near this place which goes over petrified sand dunes is called the Slickrock Trail. A mysterious triangular metal pillar was discovered in a slot canyon near this city in 2020. Courthouse Towers and the Phallus Pillar are rock formations near this city, which lies across the Colorado River from Arches National Park. For 10 points, name this most populous city in the Canyonlands of eastern Utah.

Using his connections with the son of a local politician, Belgian businessman Édouard Empain held a "Great Week of Aviation" to advertise his construction of a new neighborhood of this city. Some have speculated that the short time frame during which fires started at places like the Shepheard's and Excelsior Hotels is evidence that an anti-imperial riot in this city was an organized plot. A law school in this city was identified as vital to sustaining the British presence there in a book by Alfred Milner, a presence he called a "veiled protectorate". This was the [emphasize] largest city to see protests in response to the exile of Saad Zaghloul. In 1922, an early feminist and independence activist living in this city famously removed her veil in its train station; that woman was (*) Huda Sha'arawi. The capture of this city following the Battle of Tell el Kebir brought its country under de facto British control. For 10 points, which city was the seat of power for both the British-controlled Muhammad Ali Dynasty and the Free Officers Movement that deposed it?

this structure is essential for lung lobes and segments. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in lung lobes and segments.

tossups.text: The name of this disease was coined by Eugene Bleuler, while Kurt Schneider listed what he considered unique symptoms of this disease. Symptoms of this disease can be experienced by individuals taking levodopa for Parkinson's disease. That is because this disease's positive symptoms may be caused by systems in the mesolimbic pathway for dopamine. Symptoms of this disease include at least six months of disorganized speech, blunted affect, and alogia with at least one month of symptoms, and its varieties include catatonic and paranoid. For 10 points, name this disease often confused with multiple personality disorder.

While serving as Chancellor of the Exchequer under Stanley Baldwin, his man controversially returned his country to the gold standard. As Lord of the Admiralty, he oversaw the disastrous Gallipoli landings during World War One. He said "I have nothing to offer but blood, toil, tears, and sweat" in his first speech in his highest office, and he reached that post upon the resignation of Neville Chamberlain. For 10 points, name this Prime Minister of Britain during World War II.

The name of a hilly area called The Kilmog corrupted a phrase from this language for a species of broom tea-tree. A region named in this language is home to the Clutha River, which provides hydroelectric power to Oamaru. The piopio bird inspired a name in this language for the fjord Piopiotahi. Since some dialects of this language merge "ng" with "k," Kāi Tahu and Ngāi Tahu are both terms for one iwi. The Hooker Glacier borders a mountain named "Cloud-piercer" in this language, alternatively known as Mount Cook. In 2015, the Black Caps played for the first time under a name in this language translated as "land of the long white cloud." For 10 points, give this language of the name Aotearoa that activists have fought to restore for New Zealand.

This quantity appears in the denominator of the critical temperature but [emphasize] not the critical pressure in the van der Waals definition. Trouton's rule approximates the entropy of vaporization of many liquids as approximately 10.5 times this quantity. This quantity was formerly obtained from measuring the speed of sound in argon at the triple point of water. Mayer's relation equates this quantity with the difference in two types of molar heat capacities. The negative product of this quantity, temperature, and the natural log of the equilibrium constant gives the change in Gibbs free energy at standard conditions. This quantity equals the product of Boltzmann's constant and Avogadro's number. For 10 points, name this constant equal to 8.314 joules per mole kelvin, symbolized R.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for cardiac cycle. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this systole-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The systole is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in cardiac cycle.

tossups.text: One poet from this state repeated the refrain "we are in the middle of the ocean" in his poem The Slave Ship from his collection TheSlaves. A biography of that "Condor poet" by another writer from this state was titled The ABC of Castro Alves. This state is home to Antonio Balduino who is kicked out of the house of a white family after being accused of harming Lindinalva and later reignites his friendship with the non-christian priest Jubiaba. Euclides da Cunha's memoir Rebellion in the Backlands forms the basis for a Mario Vargas Llosa novel set in this state, The War at the End of the World. The protagonist of another book set in this state uses her cooking school to support her husband Vadihno until his death dancing the samba, one year before their romance is reignited. For 10 points, name this Brazilian state whose capital of Salvador is the setting of many of Jorge Amado's books, the heartland of Afro-brazilian culture.

According to the efficiency wage hypothesis, market wages exceeding the equilibrium wage tend to increase this quantity. The natural rate hypothesis claims that there is always a base level for this quantity in the market. Okun's law posits that a one percent increase in this quantity leads to a two percent decrease in GDP. The Phillips Curve demonstrates an inverse relationship between this quantity and inflation. There are cyclical and frictional varieties of this concept. For 10 points, identify this economic concept in which people in the labor force are unable to find jobs.

This location's name comes from the Miwok tribe, which was driven out by settlers in the 19th century. Galen Clark was the first Englishman to discover a hidden grove of trees at this location, which he would work to preserve for the next 24 years. Mount Lyell of the Cathedral Range is the tallest peak in this region. That range is immediately south of the Tuolumne River, which was dammed at Hetch Hetchy Valley despite the opposition of John Muir. He headed a movement to turn this region into a national park, which Theodore Roosevelt approved in 1890. Ansel Adams photographed this park's Half Dome and El Capitan monoliths. For 10 points, name this national park in the Sierra Nevada mountains of California, not be confused with the also scenic Yellowstone National Park.

This novel's main character is not allowed to go to the funeral of a yellow mule by her second husband, who forces her to wear a headscarf. Alice Walker revived interest in this novel by writing an essay about "Looking" for its author. The protagonist of this novel marries Jody Starks after kissing Johnny Taylor under a blossoming pear tree. During a hurricane in this novel, a man known as Tea Cake is bitten by a dog and later is shot by the protagonist after he comes down with rabies. That character later returns to her home in the African-American town of Eatonville. For ten points, name this novel about the life of Janie Crawford by Zora Neale Hurston.
acceptableAnswers: The Their Eyes Were Watching God

tossups.text: In this modern-day country, Fred Wendorf's team unearthed a large cow-shaped rock and cattle bones under stone tumuli at Nabta Playa. Pink teeth provide evidence for the strangulation of servants in this country as part of a retainer sacrifice performed for the dead King Aha. A bull-tailed man holds a hoe next to a scorpion glyph in a scene from a pear-shaped mace head found in this country, where false doors were placed within mud-brick tombs called mastabas. The unification of this country was symbolized by a king wearing both red and white crowns on either side of the Narmer Palette. A structure in this country named for Djoser was designed by Imhotep. For 10 points, name this country where a large ship belonging to Khufu was found near the Great Pyramid.

To protect these animals and their mustelid predator, Tonie Rocke led a three-year field trial that targeted these animals with peanut butter-flavored bait. An oral vaccine for these animals expresses the F1 and V307 antigens using a raccoon poxvirus vector. Con Slobodchikoff discovered referential specificity in the communication of these animals. The black-footed ferret is nicknamed for hunting these animals, which caused a 2003 mpox outbreak. Keystone species of these animals include one named for Gunnison and another named for its black tail. These fossorial animals do the jump-yip to bark out a "chee-chee" alarm call on their hind legs. These mammals create mounds that renew topsoil as a byproduct of digging their extensive tunnel systems. For 10 points, name these burrowing rodents named for a type of grassland.

A model claiming that information sharing reduces uncertainty which reduces the likelihood of this phenomenon was developed by James Fearon. One scholar defined "friction" in this phenomenon as real-life factors that distinguish it from theory. A Kant essay that declares "the spirit of commerce" is "incompatible" with this phenomenon is the basis of the "Golden Arches" theory which states that this phenomenon cannot occur between two nations who both have a McDonald's. This phenomenon is "the continuation of politics by other means" according to a Carl von Clausewitz work. For 10 points, the "art of" what phenomenon titles a Sun Tzu work?

A character in this novel recalls his disgust at his father's hobby of memorizing railroad timetables, after witnessing the trial of a man whom he compares to a "yellow owl". An asthma patient in this novel despises clocks so much that he keeps time by shelling beans. One character in this novel constantly rewrites a description of a woman riding a sorrel mare down the Bois de Boulogne, and dreams of a publisher declaring "Hats off!" after reading his novel. This novel ends with a dog dying in a shootout between the police and the criminal Cottard. Father Paneloux delivers several sermons to the citizens of Oran in this novel, which is narrated by Dr. Bernard Rieux. For 10 points, a lot of rats die at the beginning of what novel about a disease outbreak, written by Albert Camus?

In Cumbrian legends, this figure is a giant who founded Mallerstang Castle and tried to divert the Eden River to make a moat. He fell in love with Argan's wife, but was defeated in battle and forced to build a castle. He and his brother were exiled to Brittany and later returned to Britain to depose Constans' killer. He took his epithet from an omen of glory that appeared as a comet. He abandoned his siege of Terrabil in order to consummate his love for Gorlois' wife, going with Sir Ulfius and Merlin to find her at Tintagel. For 10 points, name this king who disguised himself in order to sleep with Ygraine and father Arthur Pendragon.

Leslie Jamison described being an actor to help people training in this profession in the title essay of her collection The Empathy Exams. A writer who trained in this profession wrote Awakenings, which became the basis for Harold Pinter's play A Kind of Alaska. An author who trained in this profession won a Pulitzer Prize for a 2010 "biography" that profiled innovators like Émil Grubbé ("ay-meel groo-bay"), William Halsted, and Sidney Farber. The book The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat was written by a man who trained in this profession named Oliver Sacks and consists of anonymous case studies like a man with prosopagnosia. For 10 points, name this primary profession of Siddhartha Mukherjee, author of The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer.
acceptableAnswers: accept more specific answers like oncologist
accept psychologist on the grounds that Oliver Sacks did some cross-disciplinary work in that field

tossups.text: A rebellion in one of this country's colonies was inspired by "magical" water mixed with oil and millet seeds. This nation dealt with the Maji Maji Revolt and recently apologized for its genocide during the Herero Wars. The Algeciras Conference addressed this country's attempt to stop a rival nation from establishing a protectorate during the Tangiers Crisis. It lessened its fight for colonies under Leo von Caprivi. The Congo River was agreed to be a neutral zone at an 1884 meeting in this country during the "Scramble for Africa". For 10 points, name this country which colonized Tanzania and Namibia and hosted the Berlin Conference.

parts.text: Name this effect, the inelastic scattering of a photon by a molecule. It typically only occurs in 1 out of ten to the seventh incident particles.

The Raman effect is useful for the spectroscopy of crystals; such spectroscopy is reliant on one of these devices, which creates a beam of monochromatic, coherent light. They are also found in CD players.
Lasers operate by creating one of these states. This state is characterized by the existence of a greater number of atoms in the excited state than the ground state.

bonuses.leadin: The surface-enhanced version of this effect relies on plasmons, and this effect generates Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of natural event, one of which formed Lake Waikaremoana, the deepest on New Zealand's North Island. The largest of these in recorded history triggered the 1980 eruption of Mount St Helens.
This human-driven activity dries out soil, lessening its cohesion and making landslides and flooding more likely. It occurs in the Amazon at a rate of a football pitch every minute.

These currents are a type of underwater landslide, and form when sediment-rich water, denser than the water surrounding it, slides towards the abyssal plain. The same name is given to this occurrence in other fluids.

bonuses.leadin: 48 million years ago, this type of event moved Wyoming's Heart Mountain about 25 miles south of its original location. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these people whose rights were addressed in the Maguire Act and the White Act. In a wave of "crimping" in the late 19th century, residents of West Coast cities were kidnapped to be sold into work as these people.
acceptableAnswers: accept Sailors’ Union of the Pacific

parts.text: An alternate term for crimping uses the name of this Chinese city as a verb. American and British enclaves merged to form an "international settlement" in this largest of the treaty ports.
Two of the most notorious crimpers shared this surname and were nicknamed "Bunko" and "Shanghai," respectively.

bonuses.leadin: Andrew Furuseth led a pair of unions geared towards these people, who could be imprisoned for leaving their workplace until 1890s reforms. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with blood glucose regulation.
What is the main function of the insulin in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to blood glucose regulation.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name this effect that results from unequal occupation of valence orbitals in non-linear molecules. This effect commonly causes tetragonal distortions that remove degeneracies, reducing the energy of the species.

Jahn-Teller distortions afflict d seven complexes with this trait, which tend to have ligands like CN that are high in the spectrochemical series. Transitions for complexes with this trait appear on the right side of Tanabe-Sugano diagrams.

Whether a complex is high- or low-spin can affect its number of unpaired electrons. Materials with unpaired electrons have this property, making them attracted to magnetic fields, in contrast to diamagnetic materials.

bonuses.leadin: It is more prominent in e g star antibonding orbitals than t 2g nonbonding orbitals. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the current White House Chief of Staff who recently called a set of liberal activists "retarded."
Emanuel apologized to Tim Shriver, the head of this charity which claims to "bring the best of sports to people with intellectual disabilities worldwide."

Eunice Shriver, a founder of the precursor to Special Olympics, brought attention to the cause through her association to this family which she grew up in. Several prominent members endorsed Barack Obama.

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions about a recent political gaffe not committed by Joe Biden, for 10 points each:

parts.text: This Semitic language which features ejective consonants and contrastive germination is the official language of Ethiopia.
This Bantu language is an official language in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. The word for "lion" in this language is the source of the name Simba.
This other Bantu language which is noted for its whistled sibilants is spoken mainly in Zimbabwe, and includes the Karanga and Zezuru dialects.

bonuses.leadin: Name some African languages, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this quantity that is proportional to distance within a parallel plate capacitor. It has units of joules per Coulomb.
Electric potential is constant along the surfaces of these materials. Electrons are allowed to move freely within these materials.

The Laplacian of the electric potential equals negative one times charge density divided by this constant. This constant has units of farads per meter, and the constant factor found in Coulomb's law equals one over the product of four pi and this constant.

bonuses.leadin: This quantity is defined as the work needed to bring a test charge in from infinity. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with portal systems.
What is the main function of the systole in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to portal systems.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this play narrated by Tom Wingfield, who describes a disastrous night involving his sister Laura.
In the climactic last scene of The Glass Menagerie, Tom tells Laura to blow out her candles, because "nowadays the world is lit by" this phenomenon, instead.
Christopher Durang parodied The Glass Menagerie in this one-act play, in which Amanda tries to find a "feminine caller" for her son Lawrence, who collects cocktail stirrers.
parts.answer: For Whom the Southern Belle Tolls
acceptableAnswers: For Whom the Southern Belle Tolls
The For Whom the Southern Belle Tolls

bonuses.leadin: This play's narrator works in a shoe warehouse with Jim O'Connor, whom another character characterizes as a "gentleman caller." For 10 points each:

parts.text: In this game, although the Pareto-optimal scenario occurs when both players cooperate, each player's expected payoff for defection is always higher than for cooperation, leading to a Nash equilibrium if both players defect.

This game, although superficially similar to the prisoner's dilemma, has a higher negative payoff to both players defecting, such that neither player has a dominant strategy. It can be used to model mutually-assured destruction, and one version of it is famously shown in Rebel Without a Cause.
This game, described by Rousseau as a story about two men participating in the eponymous sporting event, has two Nash equilibria, which occur either when both players cooperate or when both defect.

bonuses.leadin: Name these games from game theory, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this peninsula that comprises most of Denmark's land. This peninsula is separated from Sweden by the Kattegat Bay.
This capital of Denmark is not located on the Jutland Peninsula, but is instead on Zealand Island. It is connected to the Swedish city of Malmö by the Øresund Bridge.
The Little Belt separates Denmark from this Danish island that contains the city of Odense. This island was the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.

bonuses.leadin: This peninsula contains the cities of Aarhus and Aalborg. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this character whose fellow pickpockets and petty criminals include Monks, Fagin, and the Artful Dodger. He famously demands for "some more" gruel.
This author of Oliver Twist wrote about Sidney Carton and Charles Darnier in A Tale of Two Cities and about the title character's eventual marriage to Agnes in David Copperfield.

In this Dickens novel, the title character's father William and her eventual husband Arthur Clennam both serve time in Marshalsea debtor's prison. At the end of the novel, Amy discovers that she is heir to an enormous fortune.

bonuses.leadin: This character is framed by Charley Bates for stealing Mr. Brownlow's handkerchief. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Roman emperor consolidated his power with victories over Licinius and Maxentius. His belief that the latter victory was due to God led to his promotion of Christianity and his title "the Great".
Two advisors to Constantine had this name. The one from Caesarea wrote histories like the Chronicon.
A major event of Justinian's reign was this 532 revolt that was suppressed by Belisarius.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the early years of the Byzantine empire, For 10 points each.

parts.text: Identify these dark matter candidates, so named because they do not interact through either the strong or the electromagnetic force.

This adjective is used to describe the type of dark matter which WIMPs are thought to represent. This term refers to the fact that unlike other candidates such as neutrinos, WIMPs are non-relativistic.

The dark matter gravitational background formed by WIMPs gives rise to this process, which proceeds in a hierarchical fashion and is described by the Press-Schechter formalism. The end result of this process are objects such as galaxy clusters with large voids between them.

bonuses.leadin: These particles are predicted to have a mass on the order of 100 GeV, and the LuX experiment in South Dakota's Homestake mine is one of many direct detection experiments searching for them. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this psychologist, who had children observe an individual yell "sock him" as the individual punched the namesake toy in the Bobo Doll experiment.

Bandura's discovery that violence could be learned through observation contradicted this school of psychology, whose proponents, like B. F. Skinner, emphasized the role of reward and punishment in learning.

Children developed aggressive attitudes towards the opposing "out-group" in this psychology experiment conducted by Muzafer Sherif. It was conducted in a namesake state park and tested realistic conflict theory.

bonuses.leadin: This psychologist introduced the idea of "self-efficacy," or the belief that one can achieve one's own goals. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poet who described his imprisonment in The True Confessions of an Albino Terrorist. Along with Ingrid Jonker, this author was involved in a dissident literary movement whose name means "The Sixtiers."

Another member of the Sestigers, André Brink, depicted the sale of one of these locations in the novel Rumours of Rain. In another novel, Jacobus finds a dead body at one of these locations owned by Mehring.
This author depicted racial tensions on Mehring's farm in The Conservationist. This South African author also imagined the end of apartheid in her novel July's People.

bonuses.leadin: While in prison, this author meditated on his poetry in the poem "Ballade of Unfaithful Lovers." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this being who was buried under Etna as punishment for a conflict in which he participated along with his brothers, who included Porphyrion and Alcyoneus.
Enceladus was one of these beings, who were birthed by Ge the earth mother in order to avenge the imprisonment of her children the Titans after the Titanomachia.

This name is shared by both a giant who joined Enceladus and the others in the Gigantomachia and one of the Aloeidae, the brother of Otus, who sought to reach Olympus by piling Mount Pelion on top of Mount Ossa and then rape Hera and Artemis. They may have been the same being.

bonuses.leadin: This figure is not Typhon, but according to Apollodorus, he is buried under Mount Etna, which erupts when he moves. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this detective who rationalized that Madame L'Espanye and her daughter were murdered by orangutans based on disagreeing accounts of the culprits' language in "The Murders in the Rue Morgue".

C. Auguste Dupin was created by this author, a pioneer in detective fiction, who in addition to "The Murders in the Rue Morgue", wrote about William Legrand's use of "The Gold Bug" to discover Captain Kidd's treasure.

The narrator of this Poe short story is disturbed by an old man's blue "vulture eye". The narrator smothers the old man and buries him under the floorboards only to confess his crime to the police in this short story.

bonuses.leadin: This character probably influenced the later creation of Sherlock Holmes. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this campaign whose disastrous result occurred after a meeting with Philip of Swabia, the taking of Zara at the behest of Enrico Dandolo, and an attempt to overthrow Alexius III.

Much to Innocent III's horror, the Fourth Crusade resulted in the sacking of the Byzantine capital, which was notably held by Christians. Baldwin of Flanders eventually took over control of the city before being massacred by Kaloyan.
The intended target of the Fourth Crusade had been Cairo, the center of this Muslim kingdom founded by Saladin. It ended when Turanshah and Shajar al-Durr lost control to the Mamelukes.

bonuses.leadin: Fulk of Neuilly agitated for this event. For 10 points each:
